questions.stem: Which pair of places is joined by the trans-continental Trans-Canadian Railway?
options: St Petersburg and Vladivostok across the Russian lands of Europe and Asia
Paris and Istanbul through central Europe on the Orient Express line
Halifax on the Atlantic coast and Vancouver on the Pacific coast
questions.explanation: The Trans-Canadian Railway is a trans-continental line that runs from the Atlantic coast at Halifax to the Pacific coast at Vancouver. The other pairs belong to the Trans-Australian, Trans-Siberian and Orient Express routes respectively.

optionRationale.1: Sydney to Perth is the Trans-Australian route.
optionRationale.2: St Petersburg to Vladivostok is the Trans-Siberian route.
optionRationale.3: Paris to Istanbul is the Orient Express route.

questions.stem: The busiest sea route of the world, linking industrially advanced North America and Europe, is the
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic sea route links the eastern United States and Canada with western Europe. Both regions are highly industrialised and rich in trade, so this is the busiest ocean route. The other routes carry far less traffic.

optionRationale.1: The Cape route carries much less traffic and is mainly an alternative to the Suez route.
optionRationale.3: The southern Pacific route is thinly used compared with the North Atlantic.
optionRationale.4: The Arctic route is limited by ice and carries little traffic.

questions.stem: Match the railway in List-I with the places it connects in List-II.
questions.explanation: The Trans-Canadian line runs from Halifax to Vancouver, the Orient Express from Paris to Istanbul, the Trans-Australian line from Sydney to Perth and the Trans-Siberian line from St Petersburg to Vladivostok. So A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

optionRationale.2: This code swaps the Canadian line with the Orient Express and the Australian line with the Siberian one.
optionRationale.3: This code gives the Canadian line the Sydney-Perth route.
optionRationale.4: This code gives the Orient Express the Sydney-Perth route.

questions.objective: Match trans-continental railways with their termini

questions.stem: The Trans-Alaska pipeline carries crude oil from
options: the Gulf of Mexico to Chicago
western Siberia to western Europe across the Ural region and eastern Europe
Prudhoe Bay on the Arctic coast to Valdez on the southern coast of Alaska
the Persian Gulf to the Mediterranean coast across the Arabian peninsula
questions.explanation: The Trans-Alaska pipeline carries crude oil from the oil fields at Prudhoe Bay in the north of Alaska to the ice-free port of Valdez in the south, where it is loaded on tankers. The other routes named belong to other regions and pipelines.

optionRationale.1: That route lies in the central United States, not in Alaska.
optionRationale.2: That describes a Eurasian pipeline route, not the Alaska one.
optionRationale.4: That describes a Middle East route, not the Alaska one.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Satellite communication helps in television broadcasting and weather forecasting.
Reason (R): Communication satellites orbit near the Earth's surface, lower than the clouds.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Satellites relay television and telephone signals over wide areas and send images that are used in weather forecasting, so A is true. R is false because satellites orbit far above the atmosphere, many thousands of kilometres up in the case of communication satellites, not below the clouds.

optionRationale.1: R is false, so it cannot explain A.
optionRationale.2: R is false, so the option claiming both are true is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Recall uses and position of communication satellites

questions.stem: The Panama Canal greatly shortens the sea voyage between
options: the eastern and western coasts of the United States
the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
the North Sea and the Baltic Sea
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific oceans across Central America, so ships need not go round the southern tip of South America. It shortens the voyage between the eastern and western coasts of the United States. The Suez Canal serves the Europe and Asia route.

optionRationale.2: The Mediterranean and Red Sea are joined by the Suez Canal.
optionRationale.3: The North Sea and Baltic Sea link is another canal in northern Europe.
optionRationale.4: The Europe-southern Asia route is shortened by the Suez Canal.

questions.objective: Explain the benefit of the Panama Canal

questions.stem:
Consider the statements on water transport.
A. A navigable river needs adequate depth and freedom from rapids.
B. Sea routes do not need costly track to be built along the whole route.
C. Water transport is the fastest mode of transport.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Rivers are navigable only if they have enough depth and no rapids, and sea routes need no costly track along the route, so A and B are correct. Statement C is wrong, since water transport is cheap for bulk but slow, and air transport is the fastest.

optionRationale.1: C is false, so any option with C is wrong.
optionRationale.3: C is false and the option leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: C is false, so all three cannot be correct.

questions.stem: A port that handles a wide variety of cargo, both bulk and general, is called a
questions.explanation: Comprehensive ports handle varied cargo, both bulk and general, and so serve a wide range of trade. Oil ports specialise in petroleum, naval ports serve warships, and entrepôt ports collect goods for re-export, as Singapore does.

optionRationale.1: An oil port deals mainly with petroleum.
optionRationale.2: A naval port serves the navy.
optionRationale.3: An entrepôt port collects goods for re-export.

questions.stem: Two neighbouring countries have similar climate, similar resources and the same manufactured goods. They are likely to trade little with each other because
options: they produce similar goods and so have little to exchange
they have more differences to gain from
being neighbours, trade between them is automatically banned by international law
tariffs are always zero between neighbours
questions.explanation: Trade rests on differences in resources, skills and development, so that each country can supply what the other lacks. When two countries produce similar goods, there is little that either needs from the other, and the gains from trade are small.

optionRationale.2: Similarity in resources means there are fewer differences, not more.
optionRationale.3: Neighbours are not automatically banned from trading.
optionRationale.4: Tariffs are not always zero between neighbours, and zero tariffs would raise trade.

questions.objective: Explain the role of differences in trade

questions.stem: A country's exports rise from 200 units to 250 units, while its imports rise from 300 units to 330 units. Its trade deficit changed from
questions.explanation: Deficit equals imports minus exports. At first it was 300 - 200 = 100 units. Later it is 330 - 250 = 80 units. So the deficit has narrowed from 100 to 80 units, even though imports rose, because exports rose by more.

optionRationale.1: The deficit has not widened to 120.
optionRationale.3: The starting deficit was 100 and the new one is 80, so the order is reversed.

questions.objective: Compute a change in the balance of trade

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Singapore is a major entrepôt port.
Reason (R): The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Singapore collects goods for re-export, so it is an entrepôt port, and the Panama Canal does link the Atlantic and Pacific. But the canal lies in Central America and has no connection with Singapore's role, so R does not explain A.

optionRationale.1: The canal has nothing to do with Singapore's entrepôt role.
optionRationale.3: R is a true statement, so calling it false is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.stem: A tax levied on imported goods, often to protect home producers, is called a
questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax on imports, and it raises their price relative to home-made goods. A subsidy is government support to producers, a quota limits the quantity imported, and barter is the direct exchange of goods without money.

optionRationale.1: A subsidy is aid to producers, not a tax on imports.
optionRationale.2: A quota limits the quantity of imports and is not a tax.
optionRationale.4: Barter is exchange of goods for goods.

questions.stem: Which statement about geostationary communication satellites is correct?
options: They orbit close to the poles and pass over each place only once a year, giving no continuous service
They are used only for navigation and cannot relay television
They stay fixed over one point above the equator, so they can serve one region continuously
They are launched only from ships and fall back to the sea after a month in orbit
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits above the equator at the same speed as the Earth's rotation, so it appears to stay over one spot. This lets it serve the same region continuously for television, telephone and data links. The other statements are wrong.

optionRationale.1: Polar orbits do not make a satellite geostationary.
optionRationale.2: Communication satellites relay television, telephone and data signals.
optionRationale.4: They are launched from the land and stay in orbit for years.

questions.stem: The North Atlantic air route is among the busiest in the world mainly because
options: both regions are highly industrialised, with large passenger and cargo flows
the Atlantic is the narrowest ocean and has no ships, so aircraft have a clear sky
there are no airports in eastern North America, so planes fly over the sea
air travel is banned over the Pacific
questions.explanation: Eastern North America and western Europe are rich, highly industrialised and densely populated. Their business, tourist and cargo links generate great demand for flights, which makes this the busiest air route. The other reasons are false.

optionRationale.2: The Atlantic is not the narrowest ocean, and ships do use it.
optionRationale.3: Eastern North America has many large airports.
optionRationale.4: Flights over the Pacific are not banned.

questions.objective: Explain the pattern of air routes

questions.stem:
Consider the statements on transport.
A. Railways are well suited to moving bulk goods over long distances.
B. Trans-continental railways connect distant coasts of a continent.
C. Roads can give door-to-door service.
D. Air transport is the cheapest mode for bulky goods.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Railways suit bulk movement over long distances, trans-continental lines link distant coasts, and roads offer door-to-door service, so A, B and C are correct. Statement D is false: air transport is the costliest mode and is used for light, valuable or urgent goods.

optionRationale.1: D is false, and this option leaves out B and C.
optionRationale.2: D is false, so this option cannot be right.
optionRationale.3: D is false, so this option cannot be right.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on modes of transport

questions.stem: Match the waterway in List-I with its description in List-II.

right: I. Joins the Atlantic and Pacific oceans
II. Links the Great Lakes with the Atlantic
III. Joins the Mediterranean and Red Sea
IV. Navigable river of Europe flowing to the North Sea

questions.explanation: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, and the Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific. The Rhine is a navigable European river that flows to the North Sea, and the St Lawrence Seaway links the Great Lakes with the Atlantic. So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

optionRationale.1: This code swaps the Suez and Panama canals.
optionRationale.3: This code gives the Rhine the Atlantic-Pacific link.
optionRationale.4: This code gives the Suez Canal the Great Lakes link.

questions.stem: A cargo ship carries 2,000 tonnes over 3,000 km at a cost of 0.02 units per tonne-km. The total cost of the voyage is
questions.explanation: The total tonne-km = 2,000 x 3,000 = 6,000,000. Multiplying by the cost per tonne-km, 6,000,000 x 0.02 = 120,000 units. The other options come from using a wrong rate or from slips in multiplying.

optionRationale.1: 60,000 would result from a rate of 0.01 units per tonne-km.
optionRationale.3: 240,000 would result from a rate of 0.04 units per tonne-km.
optionRationale.4: 600,000 would result from a rate of 0.10 units per tonne-km.

questions.objective: Compute transport cost from a per tonne-km rate

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The WTO fixes the prices of the goods traded among its member countries.
Reason (R): The WTO administers trade agreements and helps settle trade disputes between members.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The WTO administers trade agreements, provides a forum for negotiation and settles disputes, so R is true. It does not fix the prices of traded goods, which are decided by markets, so A is false. It deals with the rules of trade and not with prices.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so R cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so the option claiming both are true is wrong.
optionRationale.3: A is false and R is true, the reverse of this option.

questions.objective: Clarify the role of the WTO
